- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 2–4% and add a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion buffer.  
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days, especially if sentiment > 0.2.  
- When true outcome deviates >3% from 30d forecast, check if sentiment was negative 3–5 days prior — if yes, model likely overreacted; apply downward bias correction of 1–2% to next 7-day window.  
- Model often underestimates mean reversion in 30d horizon; if 30d forecast is below 30-day moving average of history, add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to align with historical mean.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underestimate downside risk; add 0.5–1.0% downward buffer to forecast.
